title: Percentage points vs percent change: compute both
task: A rate moved from 40% to 45% — is that 5% or 12.5%? Both, and the difference matters.

excel.note: Percentage POINTS: plain subtraction of the two rates. Relative percent change: =(B2-A2)/A2.

explanation: Subtracting the rates gives percentage POINTS (45% − 40% = 5 points — the honest way to report a rate change); dividing that gap by the starting rate gives relative percent change (5/40 = 12.5% — the headline-friendly number). Both are correct; mixing the labels is how a 5-point rise gets reported as "12.5% growth". Finance sidesteps the ambiguity with basis points: multiply the point difference by 10,000 (here, 500 bps).
